name: Mellow Apricot
lede: Mellow Apricot is a soft orange, named in English for the fruit [[apricot]] and carried in our data as a traditional Japanese color, *Asagi*, whose name actually means "light yellow."

sections.title: Apricot in English, light yellow in Japanese
sections.body:
The English name is a modifier on the fruit [[apricot]], "mellow" softening its usual brightness [1]. Our library also files this hue under the traditional Japanese color list as *Asagi* (浅黄), which our data translates literally as "light yellow," a looser match to the hue than the English fruit name suggests [1]. Japanese traditional color names were not standardized the way the ISCC-NBS lists would later be; a single name could drift toward orange or yellow depending on the dye lot and the fabric [1].

Its nearest named neighbor by measured color is [[apricot]] itself, more vivid, with [[macaroni-and-cheese]], [[antimony-yellow]] and [[buff]] close behind [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match in 223 of 23,781 paintings, 0.94 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 146 [2]. That makes it more common than 65 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, found in 19 of the 1,674 paintings we have from that century, 1.5 times the expected rate [2]. It is most over-represented in paintings from India, at 3.3 times the expected rate [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, in 63 percent of the 146 paintings where it appears, ranked by lightness so varnish cannot fake the result [2].
